voyage.name: Hop On - Hop Off Boat
voyage.content: Audio track in 11 languages. Two of the most frequented stops are at the Palace, and at the Gamla Stan, right across the canal from T Slussen. The recordings on this loop service are reasonably informative.

voyage.name: Under the bridges of Stockholm
voyage.content: Departing from Strömkajen by Grand Hôtel and opposite the Royal Castle (T Kungsträdgården), this tour on both the sea and on lake Mälaren passes under 15 bridges and through two locks. Several departures every day, depending on the time of year. 1 hour 50 min.

voyage.name: Royal Canal Tour
voyage.content: Departs from Strömkajen and takes you around the eastern parts of the city, passing through the lush Djurgården canal. 50 min.

voyage.name: Historical Canal Tour
voyage.content: Departs from Stadshusbron next to the City Hall (T T-Centralen), and passes Kungsholmen and other western islands of the city. 50 min.

voyage.name: Stockholm Grand Tour
voyage.content: Combines a boat and a bus tour. 3 hours 30 min, 450 kr.

voyage.name: Stockholm Panorama
voyage.content: A tour of some major sights that departs from Gustaf Adolf Torg (T T-Centralen). 1 hour 30 min, 300 kr.

voyage.name: Talk of the town
voyage.content: Memory card for your mobile phone can be rented at several bike rentals in Stockholm. Load your mobile phone with audioguides at 56 of the best sights in Stockholm. Rent by hour, 30 kr or day 125 kr.

voyage.name: BikeSweden
voyage.content: BikeSweden offers several guided cycling tours and a variety of high quality bikes in the center of the city. Daily guided drop-in biketours form may-september). BikeSweden offers mountainbikes, children's bikes, racing bikes, trailers, child seats and city bikes.

voyage.name: Systembolaget
voyage.hours: Generally open Mon-Wed 10:00-18:00, Thu-Fri 10:00-19:00, Sat 10:00-15:00, all stores closed Sun
voyage.content: Systembolaget is the government monopoly chain for selling alcohol. The stores have a wide assortment and helpful, knowledgeable staff. Tax makes beer and hard liquor expensive. Surprisingly, high-end wines can be a bargain. Central locations include:

voyage.name: Klarabergsgatan
voyage.hours: Extra late hours: Closes 20:00 all weekdays

voyage.name: Regeringsgatan
voyage.content: The largest Systembolaget store in Stockholm, with a special selection of exclusive wines

voyage.name: Sergels torg
voyage.content: Stockholm's busiest city square. The black-and-white Harlequin concrete floor was laid in the 1960s, and while the design remains controversial, and the place used to have bad reputation for drug-dealing and violence, it attracts thousands of people daily for meet-ups, political demonstrations, flash mobs, and merchant stands. In 2018, a renovation was completed, reclaiming pedestrian space from car lanes.

voyage.name: Klara Church
voyage.content: Close to the Sergels Torg square, and one of the few buildings in the district to survive the 1960s redevelopment, this large redbrick church was built in the 16th century, following the demolition of a 13th-century nunnery. The 116-metre steeple is the second tallest in Scandinavia and one of the ten tallest buildings in Sweden, making it a significant landmark. The artwork inside includes an 18th-century altarpiece

voyage.name: Adolf Fredrik's church
voyage.content: Adolf Fredrik's church, named by King Adolf Fredrik, was built in 1768-1774. The exterior is quite intact, while the interior was radically changed in the 1890s. In the church, there is a monument to the philosopher René Descartes, who spent his last years in Stockholm tutoring Queen Christina, until dying of pneumonia. The church is known for the grave of Prime Minister Olof Palme, who was assassinated in 1986. The

voyage.name: Olof Palme assassination scene
voyage.content: On February 28, 1986, Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme and his wife Lisbeth made a spontaneous plan to go to the Grand cinema with their son and his fiancée, without calling in their bodyguards. On their way home, an unknown man came up behind Palme, shot him to immediate death with a revolver, and escaped along Tunnelgatan. The street nearby was renamed Olof Palmes gata to commemorate the victim. The police led sev

voyage.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.hours: Summer Tue-Sun 11-18, Sat 11-17, Non-Summer T-Wed 11-17, Thu 11-20, Fri-Sun 11-17
voyage.content: Sweden's national museum for European art opened in 1866. A renovation for accessibility and climate control was finished in 2018. The museum exhibits works by Rembrandt, Rubens, Goya, Renoir, Degas and Gauguin, as well as well-known Swedish artists such as Carl Larsson, Ernst Josephson, C F Hill and Anders Zorn. The museum also has a collection of applied art, design, and industrial design. The museum has a nice caf

voyage.name: The House of Culture
voyage.content: Kulturhuset, a 1970s concrete building in the middle of the modernist city centre, is operated by the city, and a venue for art exhibitions and performances. The building also houses the Stockholm City Theatre, a library (with a comic book department), a teen activity centre, and a scale model of Stockholm. On ground level there is an Internet café.

voyage.name: Mediterranean Museum
voyage.content: Contains ancient artefacts of the Mediterranean and the Middle East, with a distinguished collection from Cyprus, and an Egyptian mummy exhibition.

voyage.name: Dansmuseet
voyage.content: Displays objects related to concert dancing.

voyage.name: Strindbergsmuseet
voyage.content: Dedicated to fin de siècle writer August Strindberg. Closed Monday.

voyage.name: Royal Swedish Academy of Fine Arts
voyage.content: Free entrance. Holds several works from Nationalmuseum. At the same address you can find Galleri Magnus Karlsson (M-F 12:00-17:00, Sa Su 12:00-16:00), a small, local gallery showcasing local artworks.

voyage.name: Nybroplan
voyage.content: A square which was built in the 19th century, creating a traffic hub for steamboats to Stockholm archipelago, as well as trams. Sweden's first traffic light was set up at Nybroplan in 1924. A statue commemorates Swedish inventor John Ericsson, who designed one of England's first steam locomotives (the Novelty) as well as the USS Monitor (which was decisive in the American Civil War).

voyage.name: Great Synagogue
voyage.content: Inaugurated in 1870.

voyage.name: Raoul Wallenberg Monument
voyage.content: A monument near the Stockholm Synagogue commemorates Raoul Wallenberg, a diplomat who had 10,000 Jews in Budapest rescued from the Holocaust. Sweden was neutral during World War II, and made many concessions to Germany, including iron export and passage of German troops. As the Axis atrocities became well known, Sweden had to mend its reputation through humanitarian missions. Raoul Wallenberg travelled to Budapest, i

voyage.name: Kungsträdgården metro station
voyage.content: [ˈkɵŋsˌtrɛˈgoːɖən] Opened in 1977, and is known for its art, with elements from the former palace Makalös and other demolished buildings in the neighborhood. Due to the 1971 protests, construction was delayed, and the eastern exit was finished in 1987.

voyage.name: Hallwyll Museum
voyage.content: A museum of antiquities, many of them owned by Swedish royals and nobles. Guided tours in Swedish and English available. Note that some parts of the museum can only be accessed on a guided tour.

voyage.name: Galleri Magnus Karlsson
voyage.content: A small, local gallery showcasing local artworks.

voyage.name: Museum of Modern Art
voyage.content: Stockholm's museum of modern art is headed by Lars Nittve, formerly of London's Tate Modern. These museums have several works by famous artists - Pablo Picasso, Henri Matisse, Salvador Dalí and Irving Penn, an American photographer. Although its Stockholm counterpart might not have as vast a collection, there is still enough to satisfy both the modern art buff as well as the curious amateur. Also, the building, by Sp

voyage.name: ArkDes - Swedish Centre for Architecture and Design
voyage.content: Exhibits and models including the annual gingerbread house competition. Cafe with good views outside.

voyage.name: East Asian Museum
voyage.content: Displays ancient, classical and contemporary East Asian culture.

voyage.name: The Royal University College of Fine Arts
Fotografins hus
voyage.content: A gallery of contemporary photography.

voyage.name: Skeppsholmen's quay
voyage.content: Several heritage ships, with information plaques.

voyage.name: Kungsträdgården
voyage.content: A park with frequent stage performances, and ice skating during winter.

voyage.name: Centralbadet
voyage.content: A classical bath-house in one of Stockholm's most beautiful art nouveau buildings, this is a place where you can go for a swim, have a beer in the sauna bar or enjoy a full spa treatment. Rather expensive and sometimes crowded on weekends. Adults 130 kr (F after 15:00 and all day Sa 180 kr), includes entrance to pool, jacuzzi, gym and saunas. University students and seniors 70 kr Su–F until 15:00. Most spa treatments

voyage.name: The Royal Swedish Opera
voyage.content: This 1898 building, stages classical operas in original language or Swedish, as well as classical ballets and concerts. The first opera house was built in 1782, commissioned by King Gustav III; 10 years later he was assassinated at a masquerade ball in the same building (which was torn down in 1892). The Opera House offers daily guided tours in English. Strömterrassen is a café with an astounding view of the Royal Pa

voyage.name: Skandia cinema
voyage.content: This 1850s building houses a 1920s cinema designed by the Stockholm Public Library architect Erik Gunnar Asplund. A beautiful and intimate setting.

voyage.name: Stockholm Concert Hall
voyage.content: The home stage of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, and the place of the annual Nobel Prize ceremony.

voyage.name: Oscarsteatern
voyage.content: An art nouveau playhouse opened in 1906, which usually stages Swedish and international musicals.

voyage.name: Dansens hus
voyage.content: A stage for classical and modern ballet.

voyage.name: Hamburger Börs
voyage.content: A 200-year-old stage restaurant which has hosted world-renowned artists such as Frank Sinatra, Liza Minnelli and Rod Stewart.

voyage.name: Eric Ericsonhallen
voyage.content: Formerly a naval church, this is today a concert hall, mainly used by the many choirs in Stockholm.

voyage.name: Avicii Experience
voyage.content: An interactive exhibition dedicated to the Swedish music producer Avicii, also known as Tim Bergling.

voyage.name: Blekholmsterrassen
voyage.content: A waterfront park renovated in 2023.

voyage.name: Åhléns City
voyage.content: A large department store in a central location, with a good selection of designer clothing brands. Also beauty products, kitchenware, interior design, books, toys, and everything else you would expect from a major department store.

voyage.name: NK
voyage.content: A large, upmarket department store opened in 1915, dominated by classic fashion. Has a big book department. Well known for its elaborate Christmas display window decorations, usually revealed in late November.

voyage.name: Gallerian
voyage.content: Stockholm's oldest shopping mall, where you can find many of Sweden's major mainstream fashion chains as well as some foreign brands such as Topshop/Topman, French Connection, Esprit and United Colors of Benetton. As of 2018, the building complex is under renovation. The whole passage is open, as well as many stores.

voyage.name: Clas Ohlson
voyage.content: A large low-price electronics and DIY store. One of the cheaper options if you're looking for an electric adapter, a hair dryer or some batteries.

voyage.name: MOOD Stockholm
voyage.content: A high-end shopping mall opened in 2012, with prestige brands, contemporary art, a spa, and tree houses (!), as well as, on the practical side, free toilets that they unashamedly advertise - and rightly so, as the ones in competing establishments aren't.

voyage.name: Acne
voyage.content: Denim and some inventive young fashion.

voyage.name: Carin Rodebjer
voyage.content: Exclusive women's fashion.

voyage.name: Filippa K
voyage.content: Biblioteksgatan 2 (T Östermalmstorg), +46 8 611 88 03, Grev Turegatan 18 (T Östermalmstorg), +46 8 545 888 88 and Götgatan 36 (Man) +46 8 615 70 80/Götgatan 23 (Women), +46 8 556 985 85 (T Slussen). Everyday fashion with a broad appeal.

voyage.name: Indiska
voyage.address: Drottninggatan 53, Slöjdgatan 11 (T Hötorget or T Centralen)
voyage.content: South Asian style: interior design and clothes. There's another store at Västerlånggatan 50 (T Gamla Stan).

voyage.name: Weekday
voyage.content: Olofsgatan 1 (T Hötorget), +46 8 411 51 50. M-F 11:00-19:00, Sa 11:00-17:00, Su 12:00-16:00. Götgatan 21 (T Slussen), +46 8 642 17 72. M-F 11:00-20:00, Sa 11:00-18:00, Su 12:00-17:00. Three stores (the Drottninggatan one being the largest) with a focus on young fashion and street wear. Large assortment of the popular Swedish jeans Cheap Monday, which, surprisingly, is rather cheap.

voyage.name: Punkt Shop
voyage.content: A small store for alternative youth fashion (rock, punk, hip-hop), simple accessories, and novelty T-shirts.

voyage.name: Gamla Brogatan
voyage.content: A pedestrian street with all kinds of alternative fashion stores, including punk, thrasher and Japanese street fashion.

voyage.name: Akademibokhandeln
voyage.content: Stockholm's largest bookstore, with a large selection of books in English as well as many international magazines.

voyage.name: Bok-Skotten
voyage.content: Discount bookstore with a general selection, across the street from the Akademibokhandeln listed above.

voyage.name: IKEA City
voyage.content: The world-famous furnishing retailer has an urban store opened in Norrmalm. It has a broad product range, though not as great at the big-box stores in Barkarby and Huddinge just outside Stockholm.

voyage.name: Village
voyage.content: Furnishing.

voyage.name: Bukowskis
voyage.content: A well-renowned auction house for high-end art and antiquities, many of them on public display during daytime.

voyage.name: Lagerhaus
voyage.content: Interior design in cool retro style.

voyage.name: Orrefors & Kosta Boda
voyage.content: Flagship store for two of Sweden's most well-known glassware.

voyage.name: Designtorget
voyage.content: A design store specializing in smaller items, ranging from the beautiful to the useful to the downright eccentric.

voyage.name: Buttericks
voyage.content: A century-old store for party supplies, costume rental, and practical joke devices.

voyage.name: Kaplans
voyage.content: Vintage jewelry, watches, and silverware.

voyage.name: Cafe Panorama
voyage.content: Kulturhuset's 5th floor (T T-Centralen). A large café with large windows and a nice open terrace overlooking the lively Sergels torg.

voyage.name: Vete-Katten
voyage.content: Well-known pastry- and coffeeshop with historic interiors, dating back to 1928.

voyage.name: Fattoush / Roppongi / Panini
voyage.content: A small three-restaurant food court in a central location between the Gallerian shopping center and the NK department store. Fattoush has tasty Lebanese fast food, Roppongi has decent sushi, and Panini offers a selection of sandwiches and salads.

voyage.name: Hötorgshallen
voyage.content: Deli market in the basement of the cinema Filmstaden Sergel. Here you can get everything from sushi via meze to Swedish meatballs. Most places offer good value for money.

voyage.name: Kungshallen
voyage.content: Food court in the basement with a wide variety of ethnic foods, across the street from Hötorget. Mostly good value. Prices around 60-120 kr (dinner).

voyage.name: Max
voyage.address: Central Station (T T-Centralen), Hötorget, and Norrmalmstorg (T Östermalmstorg or T Kungsträdgården)
voyage.content: Hamburgers Swedish style. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Nooshi
voyage.content: An Asian restaurant at the centre of Stockholm, on the ground floor of the culture house Kulturhuset. The location is easily found in central Stockholm. Serves a mixture of cuisine from various Asian countries, including Japan, Korea and Thailand. 100 kr-140 kr.

voyage.name: Zocalo
voyage.content: A chain of Mexican fast-food restaurants. The restaurants are spacious and have a trendy decor. The service is based on automatic signal devices (no table service) and is very fast - getting your order ready usually takes about five minutes from when you walk in. Try the burritos, that's what the chain is known for. Five restaurants in Stockholm and four elsewhere in Sweden.

voyage.name: Sally Voltaire & Systrar
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant with different types of salads (large servings), sandwiches (not that large) and a variety of coffees, juices and craft beers.

voyage.name: Prinsen
voyage.content: An 1897 restaurant which serves traditional Swedish dishes in fine dining style, as well as some French bistro classics, all in a very nice setting. Mains 225-395 kr.

voyage.name: Eataly
voyage.content: An Italian market hall and food court inside the Röda Kvarn cinema.

voyage.name: Räkan
voyage.content: A restaurant from Gothenburg, serving shrimp and other seafood. The tables are around a pond, on which a model boat delivers the shrimp servings.

voyage.name: Café Opera and Operakällaren
voyage.content: In the building of the Royal Opera, Café Opera has for long been the place if you want to be seen with celebrities. Offers good food and drinks. Dress code applies, entrance fee 220 kr. In the same building you'll find a beautiful dining room of the formal and extremely expensive Operakällaren. If you want a less costly option, consider the other two restaurants at the Opera: Operabaren and Backfickan (see Mid-range

voyage.name: F12
voyage.content: The stylish F12 (short for the centrally located address) is regarded as one of the best fine dining experiences in Stockholm by most critics, including White Guide, the most ambitious Swedish restaurant guide. Mains 270-520 kr, 7-course tasting menus 1095 kr.

voyage.name: Frantzén
voyage.content: Only restaurant in Stockholm awarded with three Guide Michelin stars.

voyage.name: Bishop's Arms
voyage.content: There is one English-style pub in the Bishop's arms chain close to the Central station.

voyage.name: IceBar
voyage.content: The bar is made of ice. You have to wait a long time before you can get in, because there are only 30 people allowed at a time.

voyage.name: The King's Fox
voyage.content: A British-style pub.

voyage.name: Radisson Skybar
voyage.content: Not the most elevated sky bar in the world, in any sense of the word, but if you want a panoramic view to go with your drink this is the only option in the Norrmalm area (although Gondolen's Bar on Södermalm probably has better drinks).

voyage.name: Kristall
voyage.content: A three-floor nightclub opened in early 2013. Usually free entrance.

voyage.name: Internationella Pressklubben / Duvel Café
voyage.content: Boasts a broad assortment of Belgian beer. Offers beer tasting events.

voyage.name: Le Bon Palais
voyage.content: A three-floor nightclub with 1980s and 90s music and karaoke.

voyage.name: Glenn Miller Café
voyage.content: Renowned jazz club in Stockholm serving French cuisine. There is a live jazz concert in the late evenings, Wednesday through Sunday. Reservations are available for dining guests and the concert fee is a minimum of 50 kr per set and per person. Guests can also enjoy the concert with a drink in the bar. You can enjoy a variety of jazz music by artists like Max Agnas, Niklas Barnö, Kjetil Mulelid, Anders Chico Lindvall

voyage.name: Konstnärsbaren
voyage.content: Wall painting by Sweden's most famous artists.

voyage.name: Golden Hits
voyage.content: Not just a three-floor nightclub with a karaoke bar, but also a stage for dinner shows with pop music. Guests of all ages.

voyage.name: East
voyage.content: Asian cross-cooking, funky music, and ethnic diversity hardly seen at any other nightclub in central Stockholm. Open until 03:00 every night, but gets crowded, so go there well before midnight. Dress code may apply.

voyage.name: Rose
voyage.content: A dance club dominated by juniors. Hit music.

voyage.name: Tak
voyage.content: Rooftop bar with astounding view of Stockholm in all directions.

voyage.name: The Nest
voyage.content: An indoor skybar.

voyage.name: Harry B James
voyage.content: Rock'n'roll bar with occasional live performances.

voyage.name: Naglo
voyage.content: A small vodka bar with a schlager (Eurovision Song Contest) playlist, regularly visited by gay men and opera fans.

voyage.name: The Cadier Bar
voyage.content: Inside the Grand Hôtel, this is one of the more upscale places one can find in Stockholm. It has been refurbished, and offers a modern yet classic atmosphere and really good drinks at that.

voyage.name: Berns Bar
voyage.content: Berns Bar is one of the trendier hangouts in the city centre, with a nice lounge and several dancefloors. You can eat a late dinner here to avoid the high entrance fee. Otherwise, make sure to show up early (before 23:00) in order to get in with minimal hassle. 300 kr entrance and mixed drinks costing as much as 150 kr. Can be overcrowded late at night.

voyage.name: City Backpackers
voyage.content: Close to the central station. Clean and friendly, with free wireless internet and computers. Plenty of common areas to meet fellow travellers in, including a great café at reception.

voyage.name: Hostels by Nordic
voyage.content: Opened in 2010.

voyage.name: STF Vandrarhem af Chapman
voyage.price: Dorm beds from 260 kr (non-member surcharge 50 kr)
voyage.content: A full-rigged ship, known as Af Chapman for short, and an adjacent building, 15 minutes walk from the central station. You can specify whether you want to stay in the ship or on land, and it really is a spectacular place to stay.

voyage.name: Interhostel
voyage.content: A low-cost hostel.

voyage.name: Generator Stockholm
voyage.content: A super clean and well managed hostel with a small cafe and bar. From about 155 kr/night for a shared room, and they also have more expensive ~650 kr private rooms and suites.

voyage.name: Scandic Norra Bantorget
voyage.content: A large, mid-range hotel in the northern section of central Stockholm. Approximately 1 km from Central Station, 500 m from Hötorget metro station on the Green Line.

voyage.name: Hotel Skeppsholmen
voyage.content: At the Skeppsholmen waterfront, combines central location with seclusion.

voyage.name: Haymarket by Scandic
voyage.content: The classical department store PUB has been converted to a 1920s style hotel.

voyage.name: Downtown Camper by Scandic
voyage.content: An outdoor-themed hotel in an urban location.

voyage.name: Grand Hôtel
voyage.content: A Grand Old Hotel considered to be one of the most luxurious hotels in Scandinavia, overlooking the Royal Palace. A bastion of elite hospitality, this is where the top level celebrities and political leaders stay, in fact room No 702 is the astounding Nobel Room, where the literature prize winners stay overnight. Its old world luxury and sense of style is well maintained in every room, with some in the Royal Gustavia

voyage.name: Lydmar Hotel
voyage.content: A five-star hotel, and a terrace bar with view of the Palace and the National Museum.

voyage.name: Nobis Hotel
voyage.content: Branded as "Stockholm's first contemporary luxury hotel", opened in 2009 in a 19th-century building. The building used to be a bank office, known for the 1973 hostage robbery which coined the term Stockholm Syndrome. The lounge is 28 meters tall.

voyage.name: Nordic Light
voyage.price: Weekend nightly rates from 1139 kr, during the week from 1734 kr
voyage.content: Modern Scandinavian design. Each room features individual, specially designed light exhibits, which guests can adjust to suit their mood, and several have excellent views over the city centre. The hotel is in the city centre of Stockholm next to the shopping, nightlife and the express-train to Arlanda airport.

voyage.name: Hotel At Six
voyage.content: A business hotel opened in 2017.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Waterfront Hotel, Stockholm
voyage.content: Founded in 1912, previously owned by the Swedish Freemason Order, this waterfront hotel is a prominent example of Swedish architecture. Even with luggage, this is walkable from the central train station, though finding the series of escalators and walkways to get there is not straightforward.

voyage.name: Sheraton Stockholm Hotel
voyage.content: The Sheraton Stockholm Hotel is a five-star hotel in Stockholm's central business district, perfect for both business and leisure guests. The hotel offers stunning views of Lake Mälaren, City Hall, and Old Town, as well as the largest average room size in town.

voyage.name: Clarion Hotel Sign
voyage.content: Branded as a "design hotel", with bold architecture and timeless furnishings.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Royal Viking Hotel, Stockholm
voyage.content: Its amenities include free internet and a health centre.

voyage.name: Radisson Collection Strand Hotel, Stockholm
voyage.content: Stockholm's newest Radisson is a part of the Waterfront complex between the Central Station and the Town Hall across the water. The more expensive rooms offer fine waterfront views over Gamla Stan and Kungsholmen.

voyage.name: Scandic Continental
voyage.content: This hotel opened in spring 2016. Since it is integrated with Stockholm's new commuter rail station, which opened in 2017, parts of the building are still under construction. The 392 rooms have access to gym and sauna. Public areas include a restaurant, a lobby bar, and a terrace bar with an astounding view of Stockholm.

voyage.name: Stockholm Public Library
voyage.content: A 1928 building in art nouveau style with a flair of early functionalism, designed by the famous Swedish architect Erik Gunnar Asplund. The interior of the cylinder-shaped main hall is spectacular, with three floors of bookshelves covering 360 degrees of circular wall. Books (both fiction and non-fiction) are available in many languages, including English and German. This museum does actually lend books, while the eq

voyage.name: Bonniers konsthall
voyage.content: This exhibition hall, opened in 2005 by the Bonnier family, owners of Sweden's largest media empire, showcases Swedish and international contemporary art.

voyage.name: Swedish Holocaust Museum
voyage.content: Sweden's official museum for Holocaust remembrance opened its first exhibition in 2023.

voyage.name: Forskaren
voyage.content: A life science hub with The Cell, a medical science museum, and a food court.

voyage.name: Sven-Harrys konstmuseum
voyage.content: An art museum opened in 2011, in a bold brass building.

voyage.name: Bellevue Park and Carl Eldh Studio Museum
voyage.content: The park gives an astounding view of Brunnsviken, a brackish bay. The Carl Eldh Studio Museum contains early 20th-century sculptures.

voyage.name: Gustaf Vasa kyrka
voyage.content: A neo-Baroque church built in 1906. While far from Stockholm's oldest church, it is one of the largest, with frequent concerts.

voyage.name: Astrid Lindgren's home
voyage.content: World famous writer of children's books Astrid Lindgren lived in this Stockholm apartment from 1941 until her death in 2002. Open for visitors since November 2015. Reservations only. See Astrid Lindgren tourism for related venues.

voyage.name: Karlberg Palace
voyage.content: Built in 1632 and has hosted the Military Academy since 1792. The interior is usually not open to the public. The palace park is a pleasant place for picnics.

voyage.name: Vanadisbadet
voyage.price: 90 kr for adults, 70 kr for children, students and seniors
voyage.content: An outdoor bath with a swimming pool, an exercise pool, and a toddlers' pool.

voyage.name: Stockholm SPA & Hälsostudio
voyage.content: Stockholm SPA & Hälsostudio is a private day spa, and offer affordable treatments such as various massages, spa treatments, facials and much more. You can also book a duo package for you and your friend/partner.

voyage.name: Stockholms Serie & Skivhandel
voyage.content: Stock is split three ways between amounts of Swedish comic books, CDs and vinyl. SS&S is a fairly small shop though, so don't expect to get lost indoors.

voyage.name: Runtrunt
voyage.content: Medium-sized record shop with most notably, a quite extensive soul section.

voyage.name: Nostalgipalatset
voyage.content: Vinyl records, posters, franchise toys, and other 20th century memorabilia. Nostalgipalatset is by all means the biggest record store in this list, and regardless of your taste, you are almost guaranteed to find something that piques your interest.

voyage.name: Golden Oldies
voyage.content: Sells some albums, but mostly singles. A lot of Golden Oldies' stock tends to be near mint. Not everything in stock is out in the shop though, so if you're looking for something specific, you're best off just asking.

voyage.name: Skivbörsen
voyage.content: Packed full of records, but has a bit of an appearance as if a hoarder did the interior decorations. Skivbörsen isn't for everyone, but definitely offers an interesting experience while digging.

voyage.name: Hurricane Records
voyage.content: Not a huge shop, but has an interesting and varied stock, as well as friendly staff that's happy to have a chat.

voyage.name: Nu och då
voyage.content: Second-hand store.

voyage.name: Stockholms Stadsmission Odenplan
voyage.content: Sells what most second hand stores sell: Clothing, media, books, textiles, paintings, furniture, accessories, but additionally also has a decent assortment of vinyl records, as well as a small café.

voyage.name: Cafe Ritorno
voyage.content: Nice café with personal service. Small outdoor service in the summer.

voyage.name: Mellqvist Bar
voyage.content: Thought by some to serve the best coffee in Stockholm. Expect to drink while standing in this very small coffee bar.

voyage.name: Non Solo Bar
voyage.content: An Italian café whose baristas have won the Swedish barista championships multiple times. Amazing espressos and cappuccinos and a quite nice assortment of sandwiches.

voyage.name: Espresso Sosta
voyage.content: An Italian-style café.

voyage.name: Konditori Valand
voyage.content: This is an old-style Swedish "konditori" with its 1954 interior almost completely intact. Still owned and operated by the wife of the original designer, this place is a piece of living Swedish history.

voyage.name: Orontes Kebab
voyage.content: A fast-service kebab diner, mostly rather busy.

voyage.name: Green Rabbit
voyage.content: Bakery and café specializing in rye bread and organic products.

voyage.name: Max
voyage.content: Swedish hamburger bar.

voyage.name: Kimchistan
voyage.content: Korean restaurant with a taste of Central Asia.

voyage.name: Tennstopet
voyage.content: More traditional Swedish cooking. On one evening in August each year they will serve the Swedish culinary delicacy Surströmming (fermented herring). Mains 130-265 kr, slightly lower prices at the bar.

voyage.name: Peppar
voyage.content: Awesome Cajun and Creole food at decent prices. Some have argued that they make the best burger in the city. The place is especially known for having excessive decorations at all major holidays like Christmas and Halloween. They also make really good jalapeño bread.

voyage.name: Byn Creperie & Ciderie
voyage.content: Galettes, crêpes, moules and cider in an authentic atmosphere with chansons on the stereo. Mains 89-169 kr.

voyage.name: Döden i grytan
voyage.content: Like a neighbourhood Italian restaurant, but with great chefs that really know what they are doing. The winner of Dagens Nyheter's Gulddraken award 2006 in the medium-priced restaurant category.

voyage.name: Lao Wai
voyage.content: A vegan restaurant with spicy, tasty Chinese dishes, mainly from the genuine Sichuanese and Taiwanese cuisines. Authentic high quality ingredients, and excellent cooking that will appeal to non-vegetarians as well.

voyage.name: Sushi by Kyoto
voyage.content: A small sushi bar.

voyage.name: Ki-Mama
voyage.content: Sushi bar.

voyage.name: Phi Phi Island
voyage.content: Authentic Thai restaurant with great food. The location is a little strange, but that's an opportunity to get off the beaten path and see the real Stockholm. Mains 110-195 kr.

voyage.name: Haga Bottega
voyage.content: An Italian restaurant in Hagastaden.

voyage.name: Khachapuri Bar
voyage.content: A small Georgian restaurant.

voyage.name: Blique by Nobis
voyage.content: The design hotel has a lobby restaurant, as well as a rooftop bar with a full-circle view of Stockholm and Solna.

voyage.name: Claes på hörnet
voyage.content: Tracing its history back to 1731, the inn Claes på Hörnet (in literal translation "Claes on the Corner") serves traditional Swedish food in more or less modern forms. The 18th century-inspired dining environment adds to the enjoyment. The inn also has 10 hotel rooms in 18th century style. Mains 145-265 kr.

voyage.name: Stallmästaregården
voyage.content: Stockholm's oldest surviving inn.

voyage.name: Pub Anchor
voyage.content: A hard rock club open till 03:00, with a broad selection of beers. Happy hour before 22:00. Live acts or karaoke most nights.

voyage.name: Musslan
voyage.content: The "back pocket" of seafood restaurant Wasahof next door, cosy and relaxed Musslan offers the same menu, a nice bar and DJs every night.

voyage.name: Olssons Skor
voyage.content: No cover charge. Clean and relaxed. Room for spontaneous dancing.

voyage.name: Tranan
voyage.content: A good brasserie-style restaurant that opened in 1929, with a dark downstairs bar that is a popular Vasastan hangout, with a mixed crowd. Occasional live music.

voyage.name: Storstad
voyage.content: A rather large bar with a modern, minimalist interior, Storstad is a popular meeting point in the Vasastan district.

voyage.name: Bishop's Arms
voyage.content: You know what you get.

voyage.name: Cane Rum Society
voyage.content: With of Stockholm's widest selections of rum.

voyage.name: Vanadis Hotel
voyage.content: A budget hotel at a closed-down water park.

voyage.name: Hotel Micro
voyage.content: Small rooms in the basement of Tegner Hotel. They do not have windows and the bathrooms are shared, but they are very clean and new.

voyage.name: Rex Hotel
voyage.price: Weekend rates from 790 kr, weeknight rates from 1590 kr
voyage.content: North of the city center, the Rex Hotel has a trendy designer feel to it, rooms have vintage photographs and gilt mirrors against concrete walls and the bathrooms are tiled in slate. Free internet is available and staff are extremely helpful, even posting out letters and offering advice if needed.

voyage.name: Ibis Styles Stockholm Odenplan
voyage.content: This ibis Styles is in a converted historic building with a sloping roof, which resulted in quite small rooms with sometimes bewildering (and challenging) layouts.

voyage.name: Hotel Tegnerlunden
voyage.content: This comfortable hotel is located in a quiet neighbourhood near a metro station and about 15 minutes walk from the centre of Stockholm

voyage.name: Lilla Rådmannen
voyage.content: A nice, quaint hotel in the residential district of Vasastan, located right next to the Tegnérluden park. The hotel is actually located in an apartment building, where the middle two floors consist of private apartments, and the hotel rooms are on the top two floors. The hotel greets guests with a teddy bear, which you can play with for free, or take home with you for a modest price (around 300 kr).

voyage.name: Blique by Nobis
voyage.content: A design hotel next door to the art galleries. The rooftop bar provides a full-circle view of Stockholm and Solna.

voyage.name: Elite Hotel Carolina Tower
voyage.content: A 16-floor hotel that opened in 2017.

voyage.name: Swedish History Museum
voyage.content: The history of Sweden from the Ice Age (10,000 BC) to present day, with emphasis on the Middle Ages (11th to 16th centuries). The exhibition on the Viking Age was expanded in 2021. In the Gold Room, you'll find gold treasures from the Bronze Age to the 16th century.

voyage.name: Economy Museum – Royal Coin Cabinet
voyage.content: Based on a Royal coin collection, this museum tells the story of money, wealth and financial management.

voyage.name: Army Museum
voyage.content: Displays the history of war, focused on the rise and fall of the Swedish Empire during the 16th to 18th centuries, followed by Sweden's role in the shade of World War I, World War II in Europe and Cold War Europe. The museum makes a great effort of putting warfare into a broader social context.

voyage.name: Royal Dramatic Theatre
voyage.content: Sweden's national stage for spoken-word drama. The building is impressive in its own right. Guided tours in English.

voyage.name: Berwaldhallen
voyage.content: The official concert hall for the Swedish Radio Symphony Orchestra.

voyage.name: Swedish Performing Arts Museum
voyage.content: A museum which displays dance, theatre and music from Sweden and other countries. Since 2018, it has an exhibition for Swedish pop music.

voyage.name: The Royal Mews
voyage.content: Guided tours and group visits only.

voyage.name: Lars Bohman Gallery
voyage.content: A small art gallery.

voyage.name: Designgalleriet
voyage.content: A gallery that displays fashion, arts and crafts.

voyage.name: Humlegården
voyage.content: Popular for recreation and sunbathing during the short summer.

voyage.name: National Library of Sweden
voyage.content: The library is a national archive and does not lend books. However, the equally beautiful Stockholm Public Library, Stockholms stadsbibliotek (Vasastan), does. The treasure room in the basement contains the Codex Gigas and massive medieval bible taken as a spoil of war with a unique depiction of the devil.

voyage.name: Environmental obelisks
voyage.content: Since 1994, these obelisks provide a live bar chart of pollution and other parameters for air and water in Stockholm.

voyage.name: Museum of Science and Technology
voyage.content: This large museum tells the tale of Sweden's rich tradition of engineering, with objects from past centuries, and one of the server racks from a 2008 police raid against the Pirate Bay. It is also suitable for small children, with the possibility to carry out your own experiments in the Teknorama section. Admission 160 kr - children 7-18, students 19+ 95 kr. Rebates for families and when using the Stockholm card.

voyage.name: National Sports Museum
voyage.content: A small free-entrance museum in the same building.

voyage.name: Police Museum
voyage.content: History of crime and law enforcement in Sweden.

voyage.name: Museum of Ethnography
voyage.content: Etnografiska museet, with artifacts from all around the world, mostly from indigenous people. Outside the museum stands a totem pole, crafted in the 2000s by the Haisla tribe in British Columbia, in exchange for a 19th-century pole previously held in the museum, now repossessed to the Haisla.

voyage.name: Maritime Museum
voyage.content: Exhibits Sweden's long history as a seafaring nation. Remnants of the Amphion, an 18th-century Royal yacht, and a broad collection of scale models.

voyage.name: Kaknästornet
voyage.content: The 155-metre TV tower, east of central Stockholm, offers a different kind of panorama from its viewing gallery. There is a restaurant at the top as well - when booking a table in advance for a specific meal (lunch, brunch or dinner, offered as set menus) one does not have to pay the entry fee to the tower.

voyage.name: Magasin 3 Stockholm Konsthall
voyage.content: Founded in 1987 in a former warehouse in the old Freeport district, the large exhibition space of Magasin 3 houses major exhibitions by international artists, often presenting new works.

voyage.name: Swedish Veteran Monument
voyage.content: A ceremony is held here on the Swedish Veteran Day. While Sweden evaded the World Wars and the wars of the Swedish Empire are long past, many Swedish soldiers have served in international missions. The monument was erected in 2013 to commemorate those veterans.

voyage.name: Swedish Museum of Natural History
voyage.content: The museum displays animals, plants, fungi, minerals and fossils from all continents, some acquired during the voyages of James Cook. Features exhibits of evolution, the polar areas, and Scandinavian nature.

voyage.name: Sweden Solar System
voyage.content: A scale model where the Globe Arena (Söderort) represents the Sun. The Earth and Moon are at Naturhistoriska. The Globe is visible from the museum's dome, with the same apparent size as the Sun.

voyage.name: Bergius Botanic Gardens
voyage.content: Open-air gardens open to the public, as well as a greenhouse, popular during the cold season. The Victoria House is a preserved Victorian greenhouse.

voyage.name: Stora skuggan
voyage.content: A 4-H farm with a restaurant.

voyage.name: Norra Djurgårdsstaden
voyage.content: During the 19th and 20th centuries, the Stockholm Gasworks was here. The contaminated ground has been sanitized. As of the 2010s, a new neighbourhood is under construction, with sustainable waste management, and acclaimed post-modern architecture. The brick buildings remain.

voyage.name: Stockholm Transport Museum
voyage.content: The regeneration building of the gas works is used as a museum of Stockholm's public transportation system, with an emphasis on trams.

voyage.name: Sturebadet
voyage.content: The costliest, and possibly the most beautiful, spa in central Stockholm. For those who can afford it, this place offers luxury in a listed 1880s building (faithfully reconstructed after a fire in 1985). Entrance costs 495 kr (F-Su 595 kr). It includes rented towel, robe and slippers, and entrance to pool, spa-section, gym and saunas. Most spa treatments 540 kr and upwards.

voyage.name: Brunnsviken
voyage.content: A brackish bay, adjacent to the National City Park. There are several fine beaches, particularly on the eastern side (T Universitetet). Popular with students as it is less than a kilometre from the university's main campus.

voyage.name: Stockholm Stadium
voyage.content: A red brick stadium with just above 14,000 seats, built for the 1912 Stockholm Olympics. For decades the home of Djurgårdens IF men's soccer team, but in 2013, the women's team of the same club. Also hosts track and field, the Stockholm Marathon, concerts and other events.

voyage.name: DN-galan
voyage.content: The leading track and field event in Sweden, and a part of the IAAF World Athletic Tour, held annually in July in the beautiful Stockholm Olympic Stadium.

voyage.name: Stockholm Open
voyage.content: A tennis event on the ATP Tour, held in the Royal Tennis Hall in Östermalm in October, attracting many of the world's finest tennis players.

voyage.name: Magic Bar
voyage.content: This restaurant brands itself as Europe's only stage dedicated to the art of illusion. Close-up magic on weekday nights, stage shows on weekends.

voyage.name: Kampementsbadet
voyage.content: An outdoor swimming pool with a gym, open during summers.

voyage.name: Östermalms IP
voyage.content: An open-air sport park, usually open for the public. Ice skating at winter. In July-August, it hosts the Stockholm Pride festival.

voyage.name: Wikimania 2019
voyage.content: The annual conference for the projects of the Wikimedia Foundation, such as Wikipedia and Wikivoyage.

voyage.name: Sturegallerian
voyage.content: Opened in 1989, Sturegallerian is an upmarket shopping mall in central Stockholm, with stores carrying several brands, such as Björn Borg, Marimekko and Bang & Olufsen. Also the home of the upmarket restaurants Sturehof and Tures, and the nightclub Sturecompagniet.

voyage.name: J Lindeberg
voyage.content: Straightforward, casual men's wear.

voyage.name: Hedengrens bokhandel
voyage.content: A sophisticated bookstore with books in Swedish, English and other languages. They focus more on cultural books than best-sellers.

voyage.name: Svenskt Tenn
voyage.content: A well known store for high-quality Swedish design.

voyage.name: Kosherian Blecher & Co
voyage.hours: Mon Tue Thu 11:00-18:00, Wed 11:00-21:30, Fri 09:00-1 hour before Shabbat (shorter opening hours during the summer)
voyage.content: Kosherian is Stockholm's only Kosher food store. There are no kosher restaurants in Stockholm, but Kosherian offers catering and can prepare light meals.

voyage.name: Fältöversten
voyage.content: A shopping mall with mainstream stores and diners, as well as Östermalms konfektyr, with craft chocolate.

voyage.name: Planet Food
voyage.content: Although the deli market Östermalmshallen is rather upmarket and its restaurants generally on the expensive side, Planet Food is an exception, offering a decent selection of excellent and very fresh wraps for 55 kr. Salads and juices are also on the menu.

voyage.name: Restaurang Sumlen
voyage.content: In an area where sit-down lunches are expensive, Sumlen, catering to poor PhD students, offer simple but decent meals for 58 kr.

voyage.name: Chez Jolie
voyage.content: A stylish and spacious French cuisine restaurant in Östermalm.

voyage.name: Glashuset
voyage.content: A waterfront restaurant with a bar, on the walk between Norrmalm and Djurgården. Less of a tourist trap than one could expect from the location.

voyage.name: Örtagården
voyage.content: On the top floor of the Östermalmshallen food market, Örtagården serves a sumptuous vegetarian buffet with hot and cold vegetarian dishes at a decent price. There is also a "back pocket" serving meat dishes. Vegetarian weekday buffet lunch 85 kr, vegetarian weekday dinner and weekend buffet 135 kr.

voyage.name: Stockholms matmarknad
voyage.content: Premium meat, seafood, and other delicacies.

voyage.name: Ekstedt
voyage.content: A gourmet grill, recognized by Zagat and Guide Michelin.

voyage.name: Esperanto
voyage.content: Just a notch below F12 on the White Guide ranking, Esperanto offers innovative tasting menus featuring many examples of advanced cooking. Some of the best value for money in the top class niche.

voyage.name: Gastrologik
voyage.content: While lunches are 135 kr, dining menus are costly. One Guide Michelin star.

voyage.name: Grand Escalier
voyage.content: A French-style diner and bar.

voyage.name: Teatergrillen
voyage.content: A classical luxury diner.

voyage.name: Östermalms Saluhall
voyage.content: A legacy market hall in a beautiful 1880s redbrick building, with all kinds of expensive food, especially seafood, meat and cheese, as well as a food court. Re-opened in 2020 after a renovation.

voyage.name: Nymble
voyage.content: A student union with regular pubs.

voyage.name: Sturehof
voyage.content: Close to Riche, with the same owners and much the same well-to-do clientele, Sturehof's location right on Stureplan draws a slightly more mixed and relaxed crowd than many of its neighbours. The restaurant has good quality food, albeit on the expensive side. The music bar O-baren is well known for its DJ sets.

voyage.name: Brasserie Godot
voyage.content: If you fancy long drinks with a cool crowd this is the place for you. Ask for an Old-Fashioned, Godot Crush or a Bloody Mary.

voyage.name: Riche
voyage.content: Branding itself a "cosmopolitan bar", Riche is one of the most popular places with the media crowd. Two large bars, often with DJs.

voyage.name: Hotellet
voyage.content: Could be described as a hotel bar without a hotel. Free entrance, dancefloor at weekends, and a mixed crowd.

voyage.name: Collage
voyage.content: A nightclub with a rather young crowd, and an inner courtyard. The Living Room is a more intimate and funky club on the ground floor; no cover charge during weekends.

voyage.name: Stockholm Brewery Tap Room
voyage.content: Stockholm Brewery is one of the larger microbreweries in Stockholm, and they have their own tap room at Frihamnen. Collaborations with different chefs are quite common, meaning that food offerings on site differs from time to time.

voyage.name: STF Gärdet
voyage.content: A hostel just at the grassy field at Gärdet, with a beach-volleyball court.

voyage.name: ProfilHotels Riddargatan
voyage.content: A stylish hotel in Östermalm with a conference room and a hotel bar.

voyage.name: Scandic Anglais Hotel
voyage.content: Trendy boutique hotel encased in a glass exterior. In good location, combining the peace of the park with the entertainment of the city centre. Rooms are small but functional, and the hotel contains one of the most hip bars in Stockholm, always popular and only steps away from your room. The breakfast buffet lasts until 14:00. Guests are able to rent bikes from reception. The hotel has a rooftop bar with a great view

voyage.name: Scandic Ariadne
voyage.content: At the northern cruiseferry terminal in Värtahamnen. Unusually tall for a Stockholm building.

voyage.name: Hotell Örnsköld
voyage.price: Singles from 995 kr, doubles from 1495 kr

voyage.name: Villa Källhagen
voyage.content: Just outside the built-up area in Östermalm.

voyage.name: Elite Eden Park Hotel
voyage.content: Sauna, gym and two restaurants in-house.

voyage.name: Mornington
voyage.content: In a calm area.

voyage.name: Stockholm Cathedral
voyage.price: Entrance 40 kr except for visitors to services 21 May-29 Sep, free entry rest of year
voyage.hours: Open daily 09:00-18:00 21 May-29 Sep, 09:00-16:00 rest of year. Guided tours every Thu at 11
voyage.content: Storkyrkan is the oldest church in Gamla stan. Built in the 13th century in the Gothic style, the exterior was remodelled in Baroque style around 1740. The church is the seat of the Church of Sweden bishop of Stockholm. It contains two pieces of famous artwork: the 15th-century wooden statue of Saint George and a copy of the oldest known image of Stockholm, Vädersolstavlan ("The Sun Dog Painting"), a 1636 copy of a l

voyage.name: Riddarholmen Church
voyage.price: Adults 50 kr, students and children 25 kr
voyage.content: Riddarholm is the ancient core of Stockholm and this is the city's oldest building - though no longer the oldest church, as it's nowadays simply a museum. Built as an abbey in the late 14th century. Many Swedish monarchs are buried here, including Gustavus Adolphus (Gustav II Adolf) and Charles XII (Karl XII). But what about Nelson Mandela, Lord Mountbatten, Chiang Kai-shek and other notables? - No, their plaques are

voyage.name: German Church
voyage.price: Entrance 40 kr except for visitors to services 21 May-29 Sep, free entry rest of year
voyage.content: Officially named Sankta Gertrud, this Gamla stan church is the home of the first German-speaking parish outside Germany, giving some clue to the importance of German merchants in the history of Stockholm. On the site of the church, a German merchants' guild was founded in the 14th century. In the 16th century, the headquarters was converted into a church, which was later expanded. The interior is baroque in style, wi

voyage.name: Royal Palace
voyage.price: Adults 160 kr, students and children 80 kr
voyage.content: At times referred to by Swedes at the "Royal Castle". Built between 1697 and 1754, dominating the north-eastern part of the Old Town, the Royal Palace is the official residence of the monarch of Sweden. However, the Royal family lives at Drottningholm in Ekerö, using the Royal Palace only for official ceremonies. It is open to the public unless being used for a state ceremony. Entrance ticket includes The Royal Apart

voyage.name: Christina Gyllenstierna statue
voyage.content: Kristina Nilsdotter (Gyllenstierna) led Sweden's uprising against Denmark in the 1510s, after the death of her husband Sten Sture (Sweden's acting head of state). The statue was erected on the Stockholm Palace courtyard in 1912, as Sweden's first public monument for a woman. Driving force behind the statue were the defense of Stockholm (with the arms race before World War I), and the movement for women's suffrage (gr

voyage.name: Slottsbacken
voyage.content: Slottsbacken provides an astounding view of Stockholm's inner harbour. The obelisk was erected by King Gustav III as his gratitude for Stockholm's citizens, for defending the city in the war against Russia from 1788 to 1790. As of 2020, it is absent for renovation. Karl XIV Johan has a statue here. He was born Jean Bernadotte, was a Napoleonic field marshal, who became Crown Prince, and later King of Sweden. The Hous

voyage.name: The Royal Armoury
voyage.content: Located in the Royal Palace, still an independent museum. In 1628, King Gustavus II Adolphus declared that his uniform from the Thirty Years War campaign in Poland should be put on display for eternity. Since then, the Royal Armoury keeps these objects, and other Royal memorabilia, branding itself "Sweden's oldest museum".

voyage.name: Parliament's democracy exhibition
voyage.content: The Swedish Parliament celebrates 100 years of universal suffrage through a display window exhibition.

voyage.name: Stortorget
voyage.content: Stockholm's oldest square, dated back to the 13th century. While the square was used for corporal punishment during most of its history, the most infamous event was the 1520 Stockholm Bloodbath, where Danish king Kristian II (who since then has been known as Kristian the Tyrant in Sweden) had a hundred Swedish noblemen and dignitaries executed for heresy. The massacre caused an uprising against the Danes, in which Gu

voyage.name: Nobel Museum
voyage.content: Located in the old Stock Exchange house in the middle of Gamla stan, this museum has lots of material on the Nobel Prize, including videotaped speeches by laureates. Gift shop sells "Nobel medals" that are big chocolate coins in stamped gold foil, great souvenir/gift.

voyage.name: Museum of Medieval Stockholm
voyage.content: It displays the dawning age of Stockholm. Small and hard to find, it provides a good historical background to a visit to Stockholm.

voyage.name: Postmuseum
voyage.content: Sweden's only postal museum. Temporarily closed.

voyage.name: Swedish Parliament
voyage.content: Free-entrance guided tours in Swedish and English.

voyage.name: The House of Nobility
voyage.content: Presents Swedish history from the perspective of the noble estate. Though most land in Sweden has been held by peasants, the nobility dominated the Swedish military.

voyage.name: Uppland Runic Inscription 53
voyage.content: A runestone from the Viking Age made around AD 1100 and accidentally famous due to ending up in a wall of a 17th century building. The laconic inscription says Thorsteinn and Freygunnr had this stone [raised] in memory of [...] their son. There is no evidence that these people had travelled far; the few runestones that mention overseas travellers (Vikings) are much more famous. The cannon was set up in the 17th centu

voyage.name: Jewish Museum
voyage.content: This 17th-century building was an auction chamber until it became Stockholm's first synagogue from 1795 to 1870; the year when Jews got full civil rights, and the Great Synagogue was inaugurated. The building has among other things been used as a police station, until the Jewish Museum (on different premises since 1992) moved into the building in 2019.

voyage.name: Järnpojke
voyage.content: A 1967 statue which is said to bring good luck when offered coins.

voyage.name: Forum för levande historia
voyage.content: A museum with exhibitions focused on human rights and crimes against humanity. Previous exhibitions have depicted Sweden's role in World War II in Europe and the Holocaust.

voyage.name: Galleri Cobra
voyage.content: Art gallery.

voyage.name: Rooftop Tour
voyage.content: Look at Stockholm from the roofs of Riddarholmen island. An exciting experience if you're not afraid of heights.

voyage.name: Storkyrkobadet
voyage.price: Adults 40 kr, includes entrance to pool and sauna. Students and seniors 30 kr
voyage.hours: Open for men Tue Fri Sun 05:00-20:30; for women Mon Thu 05:00-20:30; closed during summer
voyage.content: A small secret hidden in what once was a wine cellar in the old town, where you can take a bath beneath 18th century vaults. Men and women cannot visit the bath together.

voyage.name: Musikvalvet Baggen
voyage.content: A cellar for intimate cross-genre concerts. The bar serves alcoholic beverages.

voyage.name: Musikvalvet Brinken
voyage.content: A second stage with the same concept as Musikvalvet Baggen.

voyage.name: Old Town Walking Tour
voyage.content: Daily walking tours of Gamla Stan.

voyage.name: Christmas fair
voyage.hours: A Christmas fair open daily 11:00-18:00 from late November to late December

voyage.name: Sweden Bookshop
voyage.address: Slottsbacken 10 (T Gamla stan or T Kungsträdgården)
voyage.content: Whether you’re looking for a Swedish cookbook, a glossy coffee-table book on Swedish design or Swedish fiction in English translation, this is the place to go. Part of the Swedish Institute, Sweden Bookshop is a specialized bookstore that supplies a broad selection of information about Sweden and Swedish literature in English and other languages.

voyage.name: Gamla stans bokhandel
voyage.content: A bookstore profiled towards history and arts. Most titles are in Swedish.

voyage.name: The Science Fiction Bookstore
voyage.content: A bookshop selling science fiction, fantasy, horror, manga/anime, role-playing games, boardgames and popular science; a lot of it is in English.

voyage.name: Castor
voyage.content: Contemporary arts and crafts.

voyage.name: Sound Pollution
voyage.content: A record label for independent rock music, with a store for LP records and merchandise.

voyage.name: Gamla stans polkagriskokeri
voyage.content: A candy factory.

voyage.name: Trafik-nostalgiska förlaget
voyage.content: A store for books, scale models and merchandise related to transportation, in particular Swedish rail transportation.

voyage.name: Coop Järntorget
voyage.content: A supermarket, with both groceries and ready-made food.

voyage.name: Munkbrohallen
voyage.content: A high-end supermarket.

voyage.name: Tasty America
voyage.content: American food and soft drinks for homesick travellers.

voyage.name: Burger King Gamla Stan
voyage.content: American fast food with great view of the square.

voyage.name: Chokladkoppen & Kaffekoppen
voyage.content: Kaffekoppen and Chokladkoppen (literally, the Coffee Cup and the Chocolate Cup) are two LGBT-friendly sister cafes situated on the Stortorget in Gamla stan, just off the touristy Västerlånggatan. If one is full you can just walk over to the other one. The interior in both of them is small but cosy, probably not for the claustrophobic! Gigantic sandwiches if you're hungry, and if you're looking for something sweet try

voyage.name: Café Sten Sture
voyage.content: A café in a 14th century cellar vault. The building used to be a monastery, until it was dismantled following the Protestant Reformation. It was used as a prison; the most famous inmate was Johan Jacob Anckarström, who assassinated King Gustav III.

voyage.name: Grillska huset
voyage.content: The medieval building was owned by the Grill family from 1681 to 1800; one of the first wealthy common families. The building has a café and restaurant run by the Stockholm City Mission, less overpriced than many other venues around Stortorget. The courtyard has a view of the Cepheus block, which had fallen in decay in the early 20th century, but was restored in the mid-20th century as a hallmark of modernization of

voyage.name: Sundbergs konditori
voyage.content: Opened in 1785 and at its current location since 1793, this is Stockholm's oldest café.

voyage.name: Café Krans
voyage.content: An independent Swedish café.

voyage.name: Café Muren
voyage.content: A cellar café with remnants of the old city wall.

voyage.name: Aifur
voyage.content: A Viking restaurant, branding itself as the only of its kind. Live Viking Age music.

voyage.name: Hermitage
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant.

voyage.name: Shogun
voyage.content: Opened in 1985, as Stockholm's first contact with the internationalized Japanese cuisine.

voyage.name: Järntorgspumpen
voyage.content: A classical diner in a 500-year old building.

voyage.name: Mr French
voyage.content: French-style restaurant on the waterfront.

voyage.name: Lasse i Gatan
voyage.content: A restaurant and bar in 18th century pirate style.

voyage.name: Leijontornet
voyage.price: Three-course dinner 745 kr. Mains in Leijonbaren 115-210 kr
voyage.content: Leijontornet is a classical fine diner, and the main restaurant in this local chain. With the foundations of a city wall tower behind glass in the cellar dining room, Leijontornet is about exclusive food with a traditionalist slant in an exclusive historical environment. The street-level bar next door is a surprisingly vivid place with cheaper dishes from the kitchen.

voyage.name: Djuret
voyage.content: Serves meat from one animal species, changing monthly.

voyage.name: Tweed
voyage.content: A British-style high-end bar.

voyage.name: Den Gyldene Freden
voyage.hours: Open Mon-Fri 17:00-23:00, Sat 13:00-23:00 (closed Mon in July and early August)
voyage.content: The members of the Swedish Academy (famous as the jury for the Nobel Prize in Literature) eat here every Thursday. Old traditions (traced back to 1722) in the old town. The reputation allows "The Golden Peace" to charge high prices.

voyage.name: Brasserie Le Rouge
voyage.content: A French-style luxury diner.

voyage.name: Zum Franziskaner
voyage.content: A beer hall which traces its history from the Hanseatic period, the name has allegedly been around since 1471. It has been at its current location since 1906 and most furniture are original. The food is classic Swedish cuisine. Also try also Bakfickan which serves beer and light meals.

voyage.name: 6e Tunnan
voyage.content: Medieval bar and restaurant, with medieval food and mead, and a small heavy-metal bar at street level. Live performances most evenings, usually Medieval-style or rock music.

voyage.name: O'Connell's Irish Pub
voyage.content: This comfortable and cosy Irish pub serves excellent pub food and has live music most nights of the week. Be sure to check out the 400-year old cellar bar.

voyage.name: The Liffey
voyage.content: A spacious Irish restaurant and pub with frequent live performances.

voyage.name: Secret Garden
voyage.content: An inclusive LGBT club with a dance floor.

voyage.name: Engelen
voyage.content: Restaurant and bar with live music every evening.

voyage.name: Stampen
voyage.content: Popular Jazz club which has been around since 1965, there's live music almost every night.

voyage.name: Archipelago Hostel Old Town
voyage.content: Central location, clean & comfy.

voyage.name: Castanea Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm bed from 175 kr, rooms from 500 kr
voyage.content: A hostel in a quiet central area.

voyage.name: Old Town Lodge
voyage.price: From 572 kr, plus 65 kr for bed linen
voyage.content: Stay in a vault of a 17th-century building in the centre of the island. Rate includes breakfast, tea and coffee all day and Wi-Fi, clean and modern.

voyage.name: Victory Hotel
voyage.content: This is the flagship 4-star hotel, with 45 rooms.

voyage.name: Lady Hamilton Hotel
voyage.content: 4 star with 34 rooms.

voyage.name: Lord Nelson Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star with 29 cabin-sized rooms.

voyage.name: Scandic Gamla Stan
voyage.content: A four-star hotel in a 17th-century building.

voyage.name: First Hotel Reisen
voyage.content: Large 4-star hotel on east waterfront.

voyage.name: Mälardrottningen
voyage.content: A private yacht launched in 1924 and retired in 1982. Upper cabins with window, lower just have porthole.

voyage.name: Sven Vintappare
voyage.content: In a 1607 building, very central in Gamla Stan.

voyage.name: Fjällgatan
voyage.content: Walking eastwards from Slussen up Katarinavägen you will reach the picturesque street Fjällgatan, with a view of Gamla Stan from the east.

voyage.name: Monteliusvägen
voyage.content: A walking path that you reach from Bastugatan (north of T Mariatorget) offers a similar view from the west. Benches and tables offer picnic possibilities.

voyage.name: Skinnarviksberget
voyage.content: A hill further west, close to the Zinkensdamm metro station, is a good option if you prefer cliffs to streets. When exiting the station turn back and head to the north. Walk up a small street to the right and climb the hill. Look for the "Kattenvägen" sign. A great alternative to watch the sun set in summertime.

voyage.name: Lundagatan
voyage.content: Preserved wooden houses from the 18th and 19th centuries.

voyage.name: Katarina Church
voyage.hours: Open to the public Mon-Fri 11:00-17:00, Sat Sun 10:00-17:00
voyage.content: Katarina kyrka ("Church of Catherine"), named after Princess Catherine, mother of King Charles X of Sweden, can be seen from many parts of central Stockholm from its location on a Södermalm hill. The church was built 1656–1695 and has been rebuilt twice after being destroyed by fires. After the first fire in 1723, the church was given a larger, octagonal tower. Following a new fire in May 1990 which left almost nothi

voyage.name: Maria Magdalena Church
voyage.content: Inaugurated in 1634.

voyage.name: Sofia Church
voyage.content: This 1902 Romanesque parish church is on the top of a hill, which is a great viewpoint in its own right. Vita Bergen is a calm park, sloping southwards.

voyage.name: Catholic Cathedral
voyage.content: Built in 1892 for the Church of Sweden. Since 1953, it serves as a cathedral for the Stockholm Diocese of the Roman Catholic Church (including all of Sweden). Most Catholics in Sweden are recent immigrants from countries such as Poland and Chile.

voyage.name: Ersta Church
voyage.content: Part of the Ersta hospital complex.

voyage.name: Stockholm City Museum
voyage.content: This building was finished in the 1660s, as Stockholm's Southern City Hall. Over the centuries, it has been used as a courthouse, a jail, an anatomic theatre, and a school. Since 1942 it is a museum, displaying Stockholm's history from 1523 to present day, with special attention to construction and architecture, and activities for children. The museum organizes walking tours.

voyage.name: Fotografiska
voyage.content: A private museum opened in 2010, in an industrial building from 1906. Besides the exhibitions, they have a diner with a great waterfront view.

voyage.name: Slussenrummet
voyage.content: A showroom for the redevelopment of Slussen (due to finish in 2025) with a scale model, multimedia, and some archaeological artifacts.

voyage.name: Ivar Lo-museet
voyage.content: A museum for Swedish writer and labour activist Ivar Lo-Johansson, famous for depicting Swedish farm workers' harsh conditions. The museum contains a small exhibition and Lo-Johansson's apartment, and requires advance booking. A scrapbook of Lo-Johansson's life is on display in the window. Across the street is Ivar Los park, a public park with a playground, and a bust of Lo-Johansson.

voyage.name: Ersta Museum
voyage.content: A hospital and nurse academy opened in 1851.

voyage.name: Anna Lindhagens Museum
voyage.content: A museum apartment in mid-19th century bourgeois style. Available to let for events.

voyage.name: Mojang Studios
voyage.content: Headquarters of Swedish video game developer studio, best known for developing the sandbox and survival game Minecraft, the best-selling video game of all time.

voyage.name: Almgrens sidenväveri
voyage.content: An original 19th century silk factory. The original machinery is preserved, and some manufacturing still goes on today. A museum displays the history of silk, from its origin in China, to the factory itself.

voyage.name: blås & knåda
voyage.content: Ceramics and glassware gallery.

voyage.name: Grafiska Sällskapet
voyage.content: The Swedish Printmakers' Association.

voyage.name: Färgfabriken
voyage.hours: Thu-Sun 12:00-18:00 (closed for much of the summer)
voyage.address: Lövholmsbrinken 1 (T Liljeholmen, Tvärbanan tram to Trekanten)
voyage.content: An exhibition hall in Liljeholmen housed in an old paint factory from 1889 (the name translates to "the paint factory"), calling itself "laboratory of the contemporary". It is perhaps one of Sweden's most interesting scenes for contemporary art. Unfortunately, it is closed for most of the summer.

voyage.name: Temporära konsthallen
voyage.content: An alternative art hall in a 16th century building.

voyage.name: GlashusEtt
voyage.price: Entrance is free during opening hours
voyage.hours: Mon Tue Thu 09:00-17:00, Wed 09:00-19:00, Fri 09:00-16:30, closed on weekends and public holidays
voyage.content: The "glass house" in Hammarby Sjöstad showcases the innovative technologies and solutions in use in the neighbourhood and is itself a very innovative building, heated and provided with energy by a selection of "green" technologies. Inside, you will find various exhibits and presentations about Hammarby Sjöstad. While most of the explanations and descriptions are in Swedish only, the staff may help you translate this

voyage.name: Långholmen
voyage.content: An island with several good spots for swimming, including a small sandy beach.

voyage.name: Tantolunden
voyage.content: A big park, known for its quaint allotment gardens, and its beach. Crowded during summer. Good for outdoor games. Also contains a miniature golf course.

voyage.name: Eriksdalsbadet
voyage.content: A public gym and swimming facility with both indoor and outdoor Olympic-size swimming pools.

voyage.name: Zinkensdamms IP
voyage.content: A soccer pitch, frozen for Hammarby's bandy games during winter. Home ground of Stockholm Mean Machines, an American football team.

voyage.name: Midnattsloppet
voyage.content: A 10-km night-time running event held annually in mid-August on the streets of Södermalm. There is plenty of live music and other entertainment along the course, creating a party vibe that draws huge numbers of spectators.

voyage.name: Victoria
voyage.content: On the lively Götgatan street, this beautiful 1930s theatre screens a broad variety of Hollywood blockbusters and classic movies ranging from the birth of cinema and onwards.

voyage.name: Rio
voyage.content: Amidst the bars of the Hornstull district, this charming independent theatre, neighbouring the LGBT-friendly café Copacabana, arranges screenings of films of all sorts - from 3D-features to festivals of low-budget shorts.

voyage.name: Folkoperan
voyage.content: Stockholm's second opera house, usually staging classics sung in Swedish, to a modernized arrangement.

voyage.name: Trekanten
voyage.content: One of the main features of the Liljeholmen borough is this lake, which allows swimming at summertime and ice-skating in the winter. The 2½-km walk around the lake is magnificent. At the half-grass half-sand beach, the water temperatures are quite high in the summers, when many are bathing in the safe, clear water. If you are visiting in winter, don't miss the hill about half way through the walk which allows sleddin

voyage.name: Hammarbybacken
voyage.content: Hosts alpine skiing in case of freezing weather (usually January-February). The view from the summit is great around the year.

voyage.name: Dieselverkstaden
voyage.content: A community centre with several attractions, including a theatre, a climbing gym and a cinema.

voyage.name: Stockholm County Museum
voyage.content: A small free-entrance museum.

voyage.name: Sickla Ovan och Under
voyage.content: An experimental mine, dug out by mining equipment manufacturer Atlas Copco. Guided tours are available.

voyage.name: Globen
voyage.content: Located just south of Södermalm, and claiming to be the world's largest hemispheric building with 110 metres across, the Globe has been one of the most eye-catching features of the Stockholm skyline since its inauguration in 1989. It was officially renamed in memory of late Swedish superstar DJ Avicii in 2021, but locals still generally call it Globen. It is frequently used for ice hockey games but also for other spo

voyage.name: Tele2 Arena
voyage.content: (T Globen/Skärmarbrink) A 30,000-seat stadium opened in July, 2013, featuring football (soccer) rivals Djurgårdens IF and Hammarby, as well as concerts and other sport events.

voyage.name: Stockholm International Horse Show
voyage.content: A major international indoor equestrian event, held annually in the Stockholm Globe Arena, featuring the World Cup in dressage, show jumping and World Cup Four in Hand driving.

voyage.name: Stockholm Skyview
voyage.content: An elevator at the outside of the arena, to the very top, with a panoramic view of Stockholm. The ride lasts 20 minutes, and costs 130 kr for adults, and 100 kr for children and seniors.

voyage.name: Emmaus
voyage.content: Second hand store.

voyage.name: Weekday
voyage.content: Large assortment of the popular Swedish jeans Cheap Monday, which, surprisingly, is rather cheap.

voyage.name: Designtorget
voyage.content: A design store specializing in smaller items, ranging from the beautiful to the useful to the downright eccentric.

voyage.name: Acne
voyage.content: Denim and some inventive young fashion.

voyage.name: Whyred
voyage.content: Laid-back minimalistic designs in low-key colors, often with some interesting details.

voyage.name: Sneakersnstuff
voyage.content: Passionate about sneakers, this store has a huge assortment of contemporary and classic designs, including limited-range models.

voyage.name: Nakkna
voyage.content: Sophisticated young fashion in low-key colors.

voyage.name: Lisa Larsson
voyage.content: Second-hand store.

voyage.name: Beyond Retro
voyage.content: Second-hand store.

voyage.name: Stockholm Stadsmission
voyage.content: Second-hand store.

voyage.name: Myrorna
voyage.content: A second-hand store run by the Salvation Army.

voyage.name: Judiths
voyage.content: Second-hand store.

voyage.name: La Principessa
voyage.content: Second-hand store.

voyage.name: Pet Sounds Records
voyage.content: A record store with independent pop, alternative rock and other genres of music with more cred than chart placements. A real institution among Stockholm's music fans.

voyage.name: Multi Kulti
voyage.content: A small but well-stocked music store specialising in the genres popularly called "world music", with welcoming and knowledgeable staff.

voyage.name: Cocktail
voyage.content: Two rather eccentric sister stores with a collection of colourful household items and other stuff. Good for small gifts.

voyage.name: Cocktail Deluxe
voyage.content: The other location of Cocktail.

voyage.name: Ringen
voyage.content: Fashion, home decor, restaurants and more.

voyage.name: Skrapan
voyage.content: A rather small shopping centre, opened in 2007, with a number of fashion stores and a rather diverse collection of other shops, in part geared towards the students living in the skyscraper on top.

voyage.name: Bruno
voyage.content: A very small indoor shopping centre with a handful of fashion stores focusing on street wear.

voyage.name: Sickla Köpkvarter
voyage.content: An enormous shopping centre dominated by major firms.

voyage.name: Globen Shopping
voyage.content: Next to the Avicii Arena, Globen.

voyage.name: Cafe Rival
voyage.content: A nice café, which like the hotel next door is owned by Benny Andersson of ABBA fame. (You won't find any traces of ABBA in the place, though.)

voyage.name: Fåfängan
voyage.content: A café and restaurant close to the eastern tip of Södermalm with a good view of the city. Music some days during lunchtime.

voyage.name: Copacabana
voyage.content: Copacabana brands itself a queer feminist café and draws a LGBT crowd from all over the city, as well as locals both gay and straight. Friendly atmosphere and afternoon sun on a few outdoor tables.

voyage.name: Vurma
voyage.content: Also on Kungsholmen and in Vasastan.

voyage.name: String
voyage.content: WiFi access.

voyage.name: Fjällgatans kaffestuga
voyage.content: Astounding view over Stockholm.

voyage.name: Älskade traditioner
voyage.content: A 1950s style Swedish café with novelty dishes.

voyage.name: Jerusalem Kebab
voyage.content: A very simple kebab bar, with great value for small money.

voyage.name: Chutney Bar & Matsal
voyage.content: Offers a choice of vegan dishes for 88 kr. Self-service salad, water, fruit tea and chutneys are free. Often quite packed but it's normal to share a table with strangers here.

voyage.name: Folkets kebab
voyage.content: A kebab diner. The buffet (open 11:00-19:00) is great, 69 kr.

voyage.name: Folkets kebab
voyage.content: Another kebab diner in the same chain.

voyage.name: Creperie fyra knop
voyage.content: Authentic French-speaking crêpes/galettes place. The place is often crowded and the service can be very French, in all senses of the word, but the food is excellent. Booking recommended. Mains 70-92 kr.

voyage.name: Nystekt Strömming
voyage.content: Typical Swedish food, difficult to find elsewhere. Fried herring in all variants, e.g. with mashed potato. Just a small stand, outside the northern exit of the Slussen metro station. Very good and quite famous! Open 11:00-18:00 in the summer, 11:00-15:00 in winter.

voyage.name: Galleria Slussen
voyage.content: Just across the bridge from Gamla Stan, has several cheap dining options, though the only one open late is McDonald's.

voyage.name: Metro Pizzeria
voyage.content: An Italian restaurant in the metro station serving pizzas.

voyage.name: Trekanten restaurant
voyage.content: Serves traditional Swedish food, located about one quarter around the Trekanten lake.

voyage.name: Max Medborgarplatsen
voyage.content: The Swedish hamburger chain which has run several McDonald's out of competition. In 2019 they opened in the middle of Södermalm, with a terrace overlooking Medborgarplatsen, as well as a vegan menu offered only here.

voyage.name: Café Eurobar
voyage.content: Russian cuisine and a meetup point for Stockholm's Slavic community.

voyage.name: Pelikan
voyage.content: Offers a small selection of Swedish dishes (including the famous köttbullar (meatballs)). The selection changes according to the season. The food is excellent and very good value for the money.

voyage.name: Svejk
voyage.content: On the cheap end of mid-range, this friendly, cosy and unpretentious Czech restaurant serves Central European fare and a wide selection of Czech beer. Great value for money.

voyage.name: Ho's
voyage.content: While Stockholm has a fair number of cheap Chinese restaurants, most serve a rather bland and watered-down version of the most popular "westernized" staple dishes. While the competition is not all that fierce, Ho's stand out as a quality choice, with a wide selection of dishes with more spice and taste.

voyage.name: Koh Phangan
voyage.content: Authentic Thai restaurant with great food. Booking recommended.

voyage.name: Hermans
voyage.content: Sumptuous weekend vegetarian buffet (theme changes weekly) followed by delicious coffees, teas, and desserts (140-190 kr depending on beverage/dessert choice). The view over Stockholm is amazing, go there at sunset and sit on the back terrace. They sometimes have live entertainment.

voyage.name: Nana Thai
voyage.content: A friendly restaurant serving delicious Thai food.

voyage.name: Nem nem qúan
voyage.content: Excellent and decently authentic Vietnamese food. Cheap lunch offers. Booking recommended.

voyage.name: Van der Nootska Palatset
voyage.content: An 18th-century palace, mainly used as a conference centre. Lunch is served 11:00-14:00, and a classical julbord (Christmas buffet) during December.

voyage.name: Hornhuset
