voyage.content: Built in 2013. Krogen is a classical diner, while Torget is more casual. Enzo's, on the top floor, is an Italian restaurant with international association football.

voyage.name: Meatballs for the People
voyage.content: A restaurant for meatballs, both in classical and luxury servings.

voyage.name: Freyja
voyage.content: A rooftop restaurant with an outdoor bar, providing an astounding view of Stockholm. Established 2023.

voyage.name: Gondolen
voyage.content: A fancy and expensive restaurant run by the famous chef Erik Lallerstedt, in the peculiar 1930s elevator building Katarinahissen. There is an inexpensive branch named Köket in the same premises where you can eat the best of Swedish cuisine for considerably less than in the main dining room, although you'll miss out on the fabulous view of the city. Dress code may apply! Mains in main dining room 185-300 kr, tasting m

voyage.name: Svartklubben
voyage.content: In contrast to restaurants with a great view, this diner puts guests in a pitch dark room. Waiters are blind. Reservations only.

voyage.name: Zee the Restaurant
voyage.content: Luxury dining with a waterfront view.

voyage.name: Akkurat
voyage.content: Friendly English-style pub offering good food, real ale, plenty of beers from all over the world as well as 450 different whiskies. A place where younger and older drinkers meet.

voyage.name: Indigo
voyage.content: A really small bar with an eclectic colour scheme, usually drawing a rather young crowd. This is a good place to start the evening.

voyage.name: Oliver Twist
voyage.content: Warm and cozy English-style pub offering good food, real ale, and other beers from around the world.

voyage.name: Patricia
voyage.content: As one of the few nightclubs open to 05:00, they have a harsh (but arbitrary) entrance policy. Dominated by gays on Sunday nights.

voyage.name: Södra Teatern Bar
voyage.content: Open Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights, this very relaxed and stylish bar offers a marvellous view of Stockholm from its lounge. Be sure to come before 23:00 to get seats offering the best view.

voyage.name: Mosebacke Etablissement
voyage.content: In the same building as the Södra Teatern theatre and bar, this is a laid-back restaurant, bar and music venue. In the summer, its large beer garden with a panoramic view is extremely popular with Stockholmers and tourists alike. Indoors, you will find lots of clubs and live music in a wealth of genres, including brunches with live jazz on weekends 10:30-03:00.

voyage.name: Sjögräs bar
voyage.content: Next door to a decent, if a bit expensive, restaurant by the name 'Sjögräs' (Seaweed), specialising in Caribbean fare, this small bar offers a wide selection of rum brands. The standard European beers are still the most popular choices for the young and rather trendy clientele, however.

voyage.name: Hernö gin
voyage.content: A bar for Swedish craft gin.

voyage.name: Carmen
voyage.content: Cheap beer, pub grub, and a lot of young broke hipsters at this Södermalm bar.

voyage.name: Gröne Jägaren
voyage.content: A sport and karaoke bar with history back to 1692. There are several other places in the hood and you will probably find a seat.

voyage.name: Kelly's
voyage.content: Cheap beer, cider and shots for as little as 24 kr each. Minimum age of 23 to enter. Hard rock music and poor acoustics. You will blend in well if you wear black leather and tattoos.

voyage.name: Kvarnen
voyage.content: A beer hall with old traditions. Popular with fans of the football club Hammarby IF. This place has expanded, adding more modern, trendy bars in adjoining rooms. Has a wide selection of beers and food at decent prices. Some scenes of the Millennium series were shot here.

voyage.name: Himlen
voyage.content: Once upon a time, the landmark skyscraper on Götgatan housed the offices of the Swedish Tax Agency. After major renovations, the building reopened in 2008, transformed into the unlikely combination of a small shopping mall, student apartments and, on the 25th and 26th floors, an exclusive-looking sky bar and restaurant offering visitors one of the most spectacular panoramas over the city. Enter from inside the Skrapa

voyage.name: Scandic Malmen
voyage.content: A hotel bar with several rooms, good for large groups.

voyage.name: Söderkällaren
voyage.content: Cheap beer and reggae music.

voyage.name: Södra Sällskapet
voyage.content: Except a restaurant and a bar, the venue hosts Sweden's most active stand-up comedy club. Showtime Monday-Saturday at 20:00. Monday shows are in English.

voyage.name: Pelikan
voyage.content: An old style working-class beer hall with a very authentic feeling, for those traditionalists who think Kvarnen has sold out. High noise level but quite a friendly crowd. Also offers simple and authentic Swedish food at a reasonable price.

voyage.name: Thai Boat
voyage.content: An outdoor boat bar, for fans of Thailand.

voyage.name: Trädgården
voyage.content: A popular summer-only nightclub, probably owing much to the fact that half of the club (including one dance floor) is situated outdoors, since Swedes love to spend as much of their brief summers as possible outdoors.

voyage.name: Under Bron
voyage.content: The winter equivalent, with alternative electronic music.

voyage.name: Sjöstaden Skybar
voyage.content: A restaurant on the 28th floor with an astounding view of Stockholm.

voyage.name: Big Ben
voyage.content: Stereotypical English pub, best known for its stand-up comedy club, with free-entrance shows in English every Thursday on 20:00. Live music at weekend nights.

voyage.name: Debaser Hornstull Strand
voyage.content: A two-part establishment at the waterfront, with a free-of-charge bar, and a nightclub that usually stages alternative concerts.

voyage.name: Slakthuset
voyage.content: In Slakthusområdet ("the meatpacking district") is, with inspiration from the New York counterpart, a nightclub for alternative dance music. With very casual furnishing, the livestock blood has barely been washed off the walls.

voyage.name: Acco Hostel
voyage.content: Free bed linen and towels, free access to computers with Internet connection in the lobby, free WiFi access in all rooms, free access to washing machine and dryer, free tea and coffee, free luggage storage room, 24/7 security observation.

voyage.name: Globen Villa
voyage.content: In this quiet neighbourhood of traditional working-class houses a welcoming lady rents 3 units for bed and breakfast. Two of the units are separate buildings, which are well equipped. The breakfast consists of several fresh things like bread, fruits and drinks. The cabins are cosy and great value. The metro is a 5 minute walk and from there 10 minutes to the main attractions. Short, the location is fine. The units ha

voyage.name: Långholmen
voyage.price: Dorm bed from 265 kr, double cell from 640 kr
voyage.content: Spectacular hostel built in an old prison where you actually stay in the old cells (making them limited to the size). The place is clean, and the staff is nice and friendly. The atmosphere is really one of a kind. It is also a hotel and the breakfast buffet holds top-standard and costs 75 kr. They have a guest kitchen, internet terminals, washing machine/dryer, and there are a lot of green areas and bathing opportuni

voyage.name: The Red Boat
voyage.content: A boat-hostel. The boat was launched in 1914.

voyage.name: Skanstulls vandrarhem
voyage.price: Dorms from 185 kr (low season), 285 kr (high season)
voyage.content: You don't require a STF card at Skanstulls vandrarhem but the prices are still cheap and the standard is higher than the STF hostels. And compared to the STF hostels, this is more flexible. Skanstulls hostel opened in May 2007 and is a clean and central hostel. Very close to popular SoFo. Book in advance since it is almost always fully booked.

voyage.name: Zinkensdamm
voyage.price: dorm from 300 kr, room from 660 kr
voyage.content: Very nice and fairly big youth hostel and hotel. It is very clean, the staff is helpful and friendly, however the rooms are rather small. Features a fairly big guest kitchen, a nice garden, Internet terminals, and laundry machine/dryer.

voyage.name: Gustaf af Klint
voyage.content: A boat-hostel with bunks and cabins.

voyage.name: Elite Hotel Marina Tower
voyage.content: In Nacka, a four-star waterfront hotel, with central Stockholm within sight and reach.

voyage.name: Rygerfjord
voyage.content: A decommissioned diesel passenger ship, transformed to a hostel/hotel, with rooms at different price levels.

voyage.name: Motel L
voyage.content: A hotel opened in 2015 in a calm neighbourhood, two tram stops from the Globe arenas.

voyage.name: Hilton Slussen
voyage.content: International business hotel with an excellent view of the Old Town and the City Hall. Sleek and modern hotel, with professional, English speaking staff. Tremendous amount of choice from fresh fruit, to cereals, fresh waffles, pancakes, pastries for breakfast. Be sure to check out the interesting wood work displayed all around the hotel, various wood types are entwined with interesting room features.

voyage.name: Hotel Rival
voyage.content: Owned by a former member of ABBA, Benny Andersson, who has restored a 1930s Art Deco red velvet cinema into a hip, elegant, and comfortable hotel. Personable staff abound, and patrons enjoy tasteful decor and bright, albeit small rooms with comfortable beds and good linens. Lobby and restaurant are trendy without being overbearing and the hotel faces a very charming city square with garden and fountain.

voyage.name: Clarion Hotel Stockholm
voyage.content: Ideal location, with lots of restaurants, a walkway along the water, and a laid-back vibe all just outside the hotel's door. Huge hotel with over 500 rooms, but the friendly staff ensure that guests feel welcomed, and there's personalized touches to be had, such as automatic checkout via email and free internet.

voyage.name: Hotel J
voyage.content: Hotel J overlooks the Nacka Strand, a haven in the far east of Nacka that is accessible e.g. using the Sjovagen ferry (line 80). Despite the closeness to the city, this area has resort-like qualities and, thanks to its steep hill rising immediately next to the lakeside, may be said to have a Monte-Carlo-like feel.

voyage.name: Park Inn Hammarby Sjöstad
voyage.content: A 15-story hotel in 2000s neighbourhood Hammarby Sjöstad, with a short tram trip to the Globe Arena, and a ferry to central Stockholm.

voyage.name: Quality Hotel Globe
voyage.content: Next door to the Globe arena.

voyage.name: Stockholm City Hall
voyage.price: Public daily tours run several times a day, 110 kr. Tours to the City Hall Tower run about 10 times a day May–September, 50 kr, tickets are only sold on the day of the visit
voyage.content: The city hall, where the Nobel Prize Banquet takes place every year, is an imposing brick building in the city centre. Guided tours are held daily, and allow you to see the impressive halls used for the Nobel festivities, the Blue Hall and the Golden Hall. The tower offers a great view of the Old Town and can be climbed (optionally, a lift can take you half the way).

voyage.name: Kungsholmen Church
voyage.content: Not Stockholm's greatest church. However, it is centrally located, still calm and secluded. Occasional concerts.

voyage.name: Stockholm Court House
voyage.content: The courthouse from the turn of the century with its massive tower is regarded as one of the foremost examples of Swedish national romanticism architecture, with a successful 2000s restoration. Open to public at weekdays; security checkpoint at front door. The building is visible in many Swedish crime dramas, including the Millennium series.

voyage.name: Kristineberg Palace
voyage.content: Built around 1750 by the merchant R. Schröder, with a beautiful park. Today used partially as a school and partially as dwelling, though you can still watch it from the outside.

voyage.name: Cheiron Studios
voyage.content: A studio where Swedish music producer Denniz Pop mentored Max Martin, and created many world hits of the 1990s. Artists including Backstreet Boys, N Sync and Britney Spears have made their master recordings here. Not open to the public.

voyage.name: Sankt Eriksbron
voyage.content: Connecting the island to Vasastan, this is the only two-level bridge in Stockholm with cars, bikes and pedestrians on the upper level and subway trains on the lower.

voyage.name: Dagens Nyheter Tower
voyage.content: Home to one of the country's largest newspapers, this used to be Sweden's tallest building for almost four decades.

voyage.name: Smedsuddsbadet
voyage.content: The largest beach in inner-city Stockholm is child-friendly.

voyage.name: Fredhällsbadet
voyage.content: A rocky beach on western Kungsholmen.

voyage.name: Boulebar
voyage.content: Food, drinks and boule pétanque.

voyage.name: Hornsbergs strand
voyage.content: An artificial beach, acclaimed for its design. Crowded at summer.

voyage.name: Västermalmsgallerian
voyage.content: Opened in 2002, Västermalmsgallerian on Kungsholmen is good-looking but relatively small.

voyage.name: Lindhagenhuset
voyage.content: A shopping mall at the front of a big parking garage, with about a dozen shops. The Thai diner at the top floor has a good view of the neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Vilse i Garderoben
voyage.content: Second hand store.

voyage.name: Café Fix
voyage.content: Stockholm's oldest coffee shop. 25 kr for coffee, 5 kr for refill. Nice food.

voyage.name: Rådhuset
voyage.content: A café inside the impressive district courthouse, Stockholms tingsrätt. A metal detector (for courtroom security) at the entrance might deter some guests.

voyage.name: Restaurang Ät Gott
voyage.content: A diner with traditional Swedish food.

voyage.name: Salt
voyage.content: A casual diner with Swedish and international food.

voyage.name: Pepe Nero
voyage.price: Virtually every meal is 95 kr, and the staff automatically supply free water, although you can order booze too
voyage.content: Half way between a fast-food place and a restaurant (looks like a restaurant but guests have to sort out their own cutlery). Does mainly Italian food, although there are also kebabs, falafel, salads, etc. Huge portions & fabulous value.

voyage.name: Mäster Anders
voyage.content: French and Swedish cuisine with an emphasis on grilled meats. Mains 145-295 kr.

voyage.name: Kungsholmen
voyage.content: Maybe on the expensive side of what constitutes mid-range, but this refined food court concept in a beautiful Kungsholmen quay location offers large portions of really tasty food in a variety of styles. Mains 175-260 kr.

voyage.name: Mälarpaviljongen
voyage.content: A self-service café at the waterfront.

voyage.name: Lux
voyage.content: In a waterside location on one of Stockholm’s smaller islands, Lux offers a relaxed atmosphere and some very good modern cooking. Mains 315-345 kr, tasting menu 940 kr. One Guide Michelin star.

voyage.name: Wijnjas
voyage.content: An old-fashioned basement with cheese and wine tasting.

voyage.name: Dovas
voyage.content: Cheap beer, 30 kr for a 500 ml bottle of Norrlands Guld or another local ale. There is a nightclub opposite which most of the young locals seem to disappear into when this place closes.

voyage.name: Theodoras
voyage.content: About 10 metres further down the street, with the same owner, it is basically a quieter copy of its brother, Dovas.

voyage.name: Nivå 22
voyage.content: A low-end pub with a roof deck, where one can drink and smoke at the same time.

voyage.name: Belman Hostel
voyage.content: A low-cost hostel.

voyage.name: STF Fridhemsplan
voyage.content: One of the largest and most modern hostels in Stockholm.

voyage.name: Connect Hotel City
voyage.price: From around 1,000 kr for a double
voyage.content: The cheapest rooms are very small and windowless.

voyage.name: M/S Monika
voyage.content: A refurbished 1908 sailboat.

voyage.name: Courtyard Stockholm Kungsholmen
voyage.content: The only Marriott hotel in Stockholm. Rooms with internet, aircon, coffee maker, ironing board, fridge and safe. The hotel has a fitness centre and a restaurant with local and international cuisine. Expensive parking at 295 kr.

voyage.name: Clarion Hotel Amaranten
voyage.content: Rooms with internet.

voyage.name: Hagaparken
voyage.content: A Royal Palace park in Solna with a rich history, open to the public, and great for picnics. The palace, Haga slott, is the residence of Crown Princess Victoria and her family. See also Swedish monarchy.

voyage.name: The Haga Park Museum
voyage.content: An indoor museum which displays the history of the Royal Park, since the 18th century.

voyage.name: Butterfly House
voyage.content: A tropical greenhouse open around the year. Except butterflies, it houses frogs, reptiles, and a large shark tank.

voyage.name: Gustav III:s pavilion
voyage.content: Open to the public during summer.

voyage.name: Norra Begravningsplatsen
voyage.content: One of Scandinavia's largest cemeteries. Among famous Swedes buried here are Prime Minister Per Albin Hansson, actress Ingrid Bergman, humanitarian Folke Bernadotte, and fin-de-siècle writer August Strindberg.

voyage.name: Ulriksdal Palace
voyage.content: A Royal Palace open to the public. An orangery with a collection of 18th and 19th century sculptures. A Royal theatre which is occasionally open.

voyage.name: Marabouparken
voyage.content: A sculpture park with an art hall. It was built for the Marabou chocolate factory.

voyage.name: Filmstaden
voyage.content: A studio complex for the Swedish cinema, closed down and converted into a museum in 1999. Ingmar Bergman has directed several films at the studios.

voyage.name: Bromma kyrka
voyage.content: Stockholm's oldest preserved building. It has also been voted the city's most beautiful church. The oldest part was built as a round church in the second half of the 12th century. The church contains medieval paintings from the late 15th century.

voyage.name: Tensta konsthall
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 12:00-17:00 (closed for much of the summer)
voyage.content: An exhibition hall in the multicultural western suburb of Tensta, opened in 1998 and has been met with much interest from critics for its contemporary art exhibitions.

voyage.name: Åkeshovs arboretum
voyage.content: A garden with exotic trees.

voyage.name: Akalla 4H farm
voyage.content: The animals are out in their pastures every day of the year. In Akalla village there is in addition to 4H-farm; Café, ceramics workshop, mini golf course, playground, barbecue area and splash pond. To get really close to the animals, you can book a guided tour.

voyage.name: T Solna Centrum
voyage.content: Countryside sceneries beneath a red sky.

voyage.name: T Hallonbergen
voyage.content: Style of children's drawing.

voyage.name: Strawberry Arena
voyage.content: A 50,000-seat stadium for association football games and other events, opened in October 2012. The arena hosts the men's national football team, as well as AIK. As of 2015, parking and roads are undeveloped, and traffic tends to be very congested before and after events. Get to the stadium early, preferably without a car.

voyage.name: Kistamässan
voyage.content: A convention center opened in 2008, hosting a broad set of events, many of them about information technology.

voyage.name: Solvalla
voyage.content: For a day at the races, you can go to Stockholm's hippodrome Solvalla, watch trotters compete in harness racing, and place some bets. Races are held Wednesday nights and many weekends. The biggest event is the prestigious Elitloppet race at the end of May every year.

voyage.name: Bodyflight Stockholm
voyage.content: Indoor skydiving facility for all ages.

voyage.name: Mall of Scandinavia
voyage.content: Sweden's largest shopping mall with more than 220 shops, opened in 2015 at Friends Arena. The cinema has an IMAX theatre.

voyage.name: Solna Centrum
voyage.content: A baseline shopping mall for everyday needs.

voyage.name: Signalfabriken
voyage.content: An indoor-outdoor mall at the Sundbyberg station.

voyage.name: Vällingby Centrum
voyage.hours: Most stores open Mon-Fri 10:00-19:00, Sat 10:00-17:00, Sun 11:00-17:00

voyage.name: Kista Galleria
voyage.content: Known for its late opening hours.

voyage.name: Rinkebystråket
voyage.content: A shopping street opened in 2016, known for ethnic food.

voyage.name: Arninge Centrum
voyage.content: A cluster of big-box stores with ample parking space.

voyage.name: Tony's Pizzeria
voyage.content: An Italian restaurant serving Italian-style pizzas and BBQ kebab.

voyage.name: Sorbon
voyage.content: A well-renowned local diner.

voyage.name: Sjöpaviljongen
voyage.content: T-Alvik, a waterfront restaurant.

voyage.name: Ulriksdals Wärdshus
voyage.content: Has high-end Swedish cuisine, and a smörgåsbord.

voyage.name: Scandic Victoria Tower's Sky Bar
voyage.content: Though the range of drinks is limited, the 34th floor skybar is the highest in Stockholm.

voyage.name: Mornington Hotel
voyage.content: A sport-business hotel near Bromma airport, with gym, massage and healthy breakfast. The airport and traffic noise at the front can be disturbing, but the hotel is at walking distance from a waterfront park.

voyage.name: Hotel Äppelviken
voyage.content: A self-service hotel in a quiet suburban neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Ängby Camping
voyage.alt: T-bana: Ängbyplan (come out of the station, turn left, keep walking
voyage.price: Tent place 225 kr, cabins from 450 kr
voyage.content: If you miss the last T-bana take night bus 198 from Sergels Torg/T-Centralen, direction Backlura, stop Ängbyplan (right next to the T-bana)) Rents out cabins, has caravan/camper van lots, and space for free camping (with plenty of shade). Spotless toilets and showers (the latter cost 10 kr). Laundry facilities, cooking facilities, internet café, mini-market which bakes its own bread and cakes every morning, small chi

voyage.name: ibis Styles Stockholm Järva
voyage.content: A relatively inexpensive hotel in an office park between the Järva Krog (motorway crossing served by buses between the Arlanda Airport and the city) and the Ulriksdal station on the local railway line between Stockholm Central station and Arlanda and Uppsala. The cheapest rooms in the hotel only have windows that face the large atrium rather than the outside, but there are no rooms with no windows as in many other ch

voyage.name: Scandic Järva Krog
voyage.content: A Scandic hotel next door to the ibis Styles Järva. Slightly outdated and stark fitouts, but no major drawbacks. Only the superior rooms have air conditioning and coffee/tea facilities, as well as irons and a maritime-themed decor.

voyage.name: Park Inn by Radisson Solna
voyage.content: The Park Inn Solna is part of the Solna Centrum and thus directly on the blue line of the T-bana. The difference between the Standard and Superior rooms is pronounced - the former are only 15 m² and fitted out as simply as possible, while the Superior rooms are 25 m² and quite modern and elegant as you would expect of a Park Inn.

voyage.name: Best Western Bromma
voyage.content: At Bromma Airport.

voyage.name: Scandic Alvik
voyage.content: A waterfront hotel 4 km from central Stockholm.

voyage.name: Scandic Victoria Tower
voyage.content: A skyscraper hotel at Kistamässan at the Helenelund railway station.

voyage.name: StayAt Bromma
voyage.content: A business hotel.

voyage.name: Ulfsunda Slott
voyage.content: A palace in a waterfront park, where each room is unique.

voyage.name: Hesselby Slott
voyage.content: Hässelby Slott, a 17th-century palace.

voyage.name: Åkeshovs Slott
voyage.content: Åkeshofs Slott, also a palace.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Royal Park Hotel
voyage.content: In Hagaparken, Solna.

voyage.name: The Winery Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with a focus on wine. The hotel has its own small "urban winery" as well as two restaurants with an extensive selection of bottles. A rooftop bar with pool is available. The hotel is located next to highway E4, so don't expect any Tuscan scenery.

voyage.name: Quality Hotel Friends
voyage.content: At Friends Arena.
